statute_title: Driving Under Influence of Alcohol or Controlled Substance
offense_class: Summary (1st/2nd, Tier 1); Misdemeanor 1 (high BAC or 3rd offense); Felony 3 (4th+)
elements: Operated a vehicle on a highway or trafficway in this Commonwealth
While the individual's alcohol concentration was at or above the legal limit
OR while under the influence of alcohol or controlled substance that impaired ability to safely drive
mandatory_minimum: 72 hours (1st offense, General Impairment); 5 days (1st offense, High BAC); 10 days (1st offense, Highest BAC or drugs)
enhancements: Three-tier BAC system: General (0.08-0.099%), High (0.10-0.159%), Highest (0.16%+) with escalating penalties
Felony 3 for 4th+ DUI offense within 10 years
Mandatory ignition interlock for 1 year on all convictions
ARD (Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition) available for first offenders
notes: Pennsylvania uses a three-tier BAC system. Refusal to submit to blood alcohol testing is treated as Highest BAC tier. ARD program is unique to PA and allows first offenders to avoid conviction.

offense_class: Summary (General Impairment Tier 1); Misdemeanor 1 (High or Highest BAC)
elements: First DUI offense within 10-year look-back period
Operated vehicle while impaired
enhancements: ARD program available for eligible first offenders: charges dismissed upon completion
License suspension 12 months for Highest BAC or drug DUI first offense
notes: Pennsylvania's 10-year look-back period applies for repeat offense enhancements. General Impairment (0.08-0.099%) first offense is a summary offense, not a misdemeanor.

offense_class: Misdemeanor 1 (2nd offense); Felony 3 (4th+ offense within 10 years)
penalty_max: 6 months (2nd, M1); 5 years (F2 if accident causing injury); 7 years (F3 4th+)
elements: Prior DUI conviction or ARD within 10-year look-back period
Current DUI offense proven under 75 Pa.C.S. § 3802
mandatory_minimum: 5 days (2nd offense General); 30 days (2nd offense High BAC); 90 days (3rd offense)
enhancements: Felony 3: 4th+ offense within 10 years
Felony 2: DUI causing serious bodily injury on 2nd+ offense
18-month license revocation for 2nd offense
notes: Pennsylvania uses a 10-year look-back period for DUI priors, unlike Illinois which has lifetime look-back.

elements: Operated a vehicle
While there was in the individual's blood any amount of a Schedule I controlled substance
OR a metabolite of a Schedule I controlled substance
OR while under the influence of any drug that impaired ability to drive
enhancements: Schedule I drugs: zero-tolerance, any detectable amount triggers highest-tier penalties
Prescription drug DUI: must be impaired, not merely presence of prescribed drug
notes: Pennsylvania drug DUI is treated at Highest BAC tier regardless of impairment level for Schedule I substances.

elements: Drove a vehicle on a highway or trafficway
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
enhancements: Misdemeanor 2 if reckless driving causes death or serious bodily injury (separate charge under 75 Pa.C.S. § 3732)
notes: Pennsylvania reckless driving is only a summary offense. Serious injury or death during reckless driving is charged as homicide by vehicle.

statute_title: Accidents Involving Death or Personal Injury — Duty to Stop
elements: Driver of vehicle involved in accident resulting in injury, death, or damage to attended vehicle
Failed to immediately stop vehicle at scene
Failed to provide name, address, and vehicle registration information
Failed to render reasonable assistance to injured persons
enhancements: Felony 2 if accident resulted in death
Mandatory license revocation
Property damage only hit and run: 75 Pa.C.S. § 3743, Misdemeanor 3

elements: Operating a vehicle in reckless disregard for the safety of persons or property
Caused the death of another person
enhancements: Aggravated Assault by Vehicle (75 Pa.C.S. § 3732.1): Felony 2 for serious bodily injury
DUI-related vehicular death charged as Homicide by Vehicle While DUI (75 Pa.C.S. § 3735): Felony 2, 3-year mandatory minimum
notes: Pennsylvania separately titles DUI-related vehicular homicide as 'Homicide by Vehicle While DUI' (F2) with mandatory minimum.

elements: Operating a vehicle in reckless disregard for the safety of persons or property
Caused the death of another person
enhancements: Homicide by Vehicle While DUI (75 Pa.C.S. § 3735): Felony 2 with 3-year mandatory minimum
notes: Pennsylvania does not use the term 'vehicular manslaughter' — the equivalent offense is Homicide by Vehicle under 75 Pa.C.S. § 3732.

statute_title: Driving While Operating Privilege is Suspended or Revoked
elements: Operated a motor vehicle on a highway or trafficway
While operating privilege was suspended or revoked
mandatory_minimum: 60-day additional suspension; 90-day imprisonment if license suspended for DUI (M3)
enhancements: Misdemeanor 3 if license was suspended for DUI with mandatory 90-day minimum sentence
Additional suspension period added

statute_title: Fleeing or Attempting to Elude Police Officer
elements: Driver of a motor vehicle
Willfully failed or refused to bring vehicle to a stop
When given a visual or audible signal to stop by a uniformed police officer
enhancements: Felony 3: crosses state line, involves accident, involves injury, driver has prior conviction

elements: While operating a motor vehicle on a highway
Consumed an alcoholic beverage
OR had an open alcoholic beverage container in an accessible area of the vehicle

statute_title: Chemical Testing to Determine Amount of Alcohol or Controlled Substance — Refusal
elements: Arrested for DUI
Refused to submit to chemical testing after being advised of consequences
enhancements: 1-year license suspension for first refusal
18-month suspension for second refusal
Refusal treated as Highest BAC tier for sentencing purposes in criminal DUI case
notes: Pennsylvania treats refusal as equivalent to Highest BAC DUI tier for purposes of grading and penalties.

elements: Knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Without a valid prescription or other lawful authority
enhancements: Felony 3: possession within 1,000 feet of school (35 P.S. § 780-113(a)(30))
Subsequent offenses escalate penalties
PA recently enacted 35 P.S. § 780-113.1 for possession with enhanced penalties near schools
notes: Pennsylvania does not use the Illinois felony class structure. Drug possession is a Misdemeanor 1 regardless of substance type unless enhanced.

statute_title: Possession of Small Amount of Marijuana
elements: Possessed marijuana
Without lawful authority under Pennsylvania law
enhancements: Felony 3 if in drug-free school zone
Possession with intent to deliver escalates to Felony 3
notes: Pennsylvania has not legalized recreational marijuana as of 2026. Medical marijuana is legal under the Medical Marijuana Act (Act 16 of 2016). Small amount (30g or less) is a separate lower-graded misdemeanor.

elements: Knowingly or intentionally possessed cocaine
Without a valid prescription or lawful authority
enhancements: Felony 3 for possession in school zone
Trafficking amounts elevate to Felony 3 or higher under 35 P.S. § 780-113(a)(30)
notes: Pennsylvania treats all Schedule II possession as Misdemeanor 1 regardless of weight, unlike Illinois which escalates based on grams.

elements: Knowingly or intentionally possessed methamphetamine
Without a valid prescription or lawful authority
enhancements: Felony 3 for possession in school zone or with intent to deliver

statute_title: Possession of Heroin or Opioid Controlled Substance
elements: Knowingly or intentionally possessed heroin, fentanyl, or opioid controlled substance
Without a valid prescription or lawful authority
enhancements: Delivery causing death: Felony 1 under 35 P.S. § 780-113.1 (Act 57 of 2014)
Fentanyl delivery causing death: Felony 1
notes: Pennsylvania has enacted specific legislation targeting fentanyl trafficking given the overdose crisis.

statute_title: Acquisition of Controlled Substance by Fraud or Without Prescription
elements: Possessed a prescription controlled substance
Without a valid prescription issued in the defendant's name
OR obtained by fraud, misrepresentation, or deception

statute_title: Manufacture, Delivery, or Possession with Intent to Deliver
offense_class: Felony 3 (small amounts); Felony 2 (larger amounts); Felony 1 (largest amounts or school zone)
elements: Manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver a controlled substance
OR created, delivered, or possessed a counterfeit controlled substance
enhancements: Felony 1: delivery within 1,000 feet of school, delivery to minor, delivery causing death
Drug trafficking in volume: Felony 1 with mandatory minimum under 18 Pa.C.S. § 7508
Mandatory minimum 2 years for heroin/cocaine over threshold amounts under § 7508
notes: 18 Pa.C.S. § 7508 imposes mandatory minimum sentences based on drug type and weight, though subject to constitutional challenge post-Alleyne v. United States.

offense_class: Felony 3 (small delivery); Felony 2 or higher (larger amounts)
elements: Delivered a controlled substance to another person
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Delivery to minor: Felony 1
Delivery in school zone: enhanced mandatory minimums

offense_class: Felony 3 to Felony 1 depending on substance and amount
elements: Manufactured or produced a controlled substance
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Meth lab operation: additional charges under 18 Pa.C.S. § 7508.2
Near school zone or in residence: enhanced penalties

statute_title: Use or Possession of Drug Paraphernalia
elements: Used, possessed with intent to use, delivered, possessed with intent to deliver, or manufactured drug paraphernalia

For purpose of planting, cultivating, growing, harvesting, manufacturing, compounding, converting, producing, processing, preparing, testing, packaging, repackaging, storing, containing, concealing, or injecting a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to minor: misdemeanor with enhanced penalty

statute_title: Acquisition of Controlled Substance by Fraud
elements: Obtained or attempted to obtain a controlled substance by fraud, misrepresentation, or deception
OR forged or altered a prescription
enhancements: Felony 3 for large-scale prescription fraud

statute_title: Possession with Intent to Deliver Controlled Substance
elements: Possessed a controlled substance
With intent to deliver, inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, currency, or other circumstantial evidence
mandatory_minimum: 2 years for heroin or cocaine over threshold amounts under 18 Pa.C.S. § 7508
enhancements: Delivery near school zone: mandatory minimum 2 to 4 years
Delivery to minor: Felony 1

offense_class: Felony 1 (Murder of the First Degree — special class)
elements: Intentionally caused the death of another person
With specific intent to kill (premeditated)
enhancements: Death penalty available for aggravated circumstances (killing of law enforcement, multiple victims, torture, contract murder)
Mandatory life without parole if death penalty not imposed
notes: Pennsylvania retains the death penalty. First degree murder requires specific intent to kill (premeditation). Life without parole is mandatory if death penalty not sought or imposed.

statute_title: Murder of the Second Degree (Felony Murder)
elements: Committed or was an accomplice in the commission of a felony
Death of another person occurred during the commission of that felony
No specific intent to kill required
notes: Pennsylvania second degree murder is limited to felony murder — killing that occurs during the commission of a felony. Subject to significant post-People v. Rosemond litigation regarding accomplice liability.

elements: Intentionally caused the death of another person
At the time of the killing defendant acted under sudden passion or heat of blood
Passion or heat was provoked by serious provocation by the victim
OR defendant unreasonably believed circumstances required use of deadly force (imperfect self-defense)
notes: Pennsylvania retains voluntary manslaughter as a distinct Felony 1 offense, unlike Illinois which subsumed it into second degree murder.

offense_class: Misdemeanor 1; Felony 3 (reckless driving or DUI contributing cause)
elements: Caused the death of another person
As a direct result of doing an unlawful act in a reckless or grossly negligent manner
OR doing a lawful act in a reckless or grossly negligent manner
enhancements: Felony 3 if death results from victim being struck by motor vehicle while defendant was engaged in reckless driving

offense_class: Felony 1 (serious bodily injury or against protected class); Felony 2 (serious bodily injury attempt or other)
elements: Attempted to cause serious bodily injury to another, or caused such injury intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
OR attempted to cause or intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to a law enforcement officer
enhancements: Felony 1: against law enforcement officer, teacher, transport employee
Felony 1: with deadly weapon against protected class
Use of firearm: additional mandatory minimum under 42 Pa.C.S. § 9712

offense_class: Misdemeanor 2 (basic); Misdemeanor 1 (fight by mutual consent); Summary (child under 12 by adult 21+)
elements: Attempted to cause or intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another
OR negligently caused bodily injury with a deadly weapon
OR attempted by physical menace to put another in fear of imminent serious bodily injury
enhancements: Elevates to Aggravated Assault (F1 or F2) when victim is a protected class or serious injury results

statute_title: Simple Assault (Pennsylvania does not use the term 'battery')
elements: Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to another person
notes: Pennsylvania does not have a separate 'battery' statute. Physical contact offenses are charged as Simple Assault (18 Pa.C.S. § 2701) or Aggravated Assault (§ 2702).

elements: Attempted to cause serious bodily injury, or caused such injury
Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
enhancements: 42 Pa.C.S. § 9712: mandatory 5-year minimum if firearm visible during assault
notes: Pennsylvania calls this Aggravated Assault — equivalent to aggravated battery in other states.

offense_class: Felony 1 (serious bodily injury threat); Felony 2 (threat of bodily injury); Felony 3 (demand by threat)
elements: In the course of committing a theft
Inflicted serious bodily injury upon another, threatened another with or intentionally put another in fear of immediate serious bodily injury
OR committed or threatened immediately to commit any felony of the first or second degree
mandatory_minimum: 42 Pa.C.S. § 9712: 5-year mandatory minimum if firearm visible
enhancements: Robbery of a Motor Vehicle (18 Pa.C.S. § 3702): Felony 1
Firearm visible: 5-year mandatory minimum under 42 Pa.C.S. § 9712

elements: Committed a robbery
While visibly possessing a firearm or other deadly weapon
enhancements: 10-year mandatory minimum if firearm discharged (42 Pa.C.S. § 9712.1)
notes: Pennsylvania's § 9712 mandatory minimums apply whenever a firearm is visible during the commission of a violent offense.

elements: Unlawfully removed another person a substantial distance from where they were found
OR unlawfully confined another person for a substantial period in a place of isolation
To hold victim for ransom, as shield or hostage, to facilitate commission of a felony, to inflict bodily injury or terrorize victim, OR to interfere with government or political functions
enhancements: Felony 1 with enhanced penalties if victim is a minor
Unlawful Restraint (18 Pa.C.S. § 2902): Felony 2 for lesser restraint

offense_class: Felony 1 (endangering persons or occupied structure); Felony 2 (property); Felony 3 (unoccupied)
elements: Intentionally started a fire or caused an explosion
That endangered a person or property
enhancements: Felony 1: fire caused death or serious bodily injury, or structure was occupied
Reckless Burning (18 Pa.C.S. § 3301(d)): Misdemeanor 1 for reckless burning

elements: With the intent to commit murder
Did any act which constitutes a substantial step toward commission of murder
enhancements: 42 Pa.C.S. § 9712: 5-year mandatory minimum if firearm visible
42 Pa.C.S. § 9712.1: 10-year mandatory minimum if firearm discharged
notes: Criminal attempt in Pennsylvania is graded one degree below the completed offense, but murder attempt is Felony 1.

elements: Attempted to cause or intentionally or knowingly caused bodily injury
With a deadly weapon
mandatory_minimum: 5 years if weapon was a firearm (42 Pa.C.S. § 9712)
enhancements: Elevates to Felony 1 if victim is a protected class (law enforcement, teacher, etc.)

statute_title: Theft by Unlawful Taking or Disposition
offense_class: Summary (under $50); Misdemeanor 3 ($50-$200); Misdemeanor 2 ($200-$2,000); Misdemeanor 1 ($2,000-$100,000); Felony 3 (over $100,000 or firearm or car)
elements: Unlawfully took, or exercised unlawful control over, movable property of another
With intent to deprive the owner thereof
enhancements: Felony 3: theft of firearm or motor vehicle regardless of value
Felony 2: theft by extortion involving threat to commit violence

statute_title: Theft by Unlawful Taking — Felony Value
elements: Same elements as theft
Property value exceeds $2,000 (M1) or $100,000 (F3)
notes: Pennsylvania does not use the term 'grand theft' — grading is based on dollar amount thresholds within the general theft statute.

statute_title: Theft by Unlawful Taking — Summary or Misdemeanor
elements: Same elements as theft
Property value under $2,000

offense_class: Summary (1st offense, under $150); Misdemeanor 2 (1st offense, $150+, or 2nd offense); Felony 3 (3rd+ offense)
elements: Took possession of, carried away, or obtained merchandise offered for sale
Without paying the full retail value
With intent to deprive the merchant of all or part of the retail value
enhancements: Felony 3 for third or subsequent offense regardless of value
Organized retail crime: enhanced penalties

offense_class: Felony 1 (occupied or adapted for overnight accommodation); Felony 2 (unoccupied structure)
elements: Entered a building or occupied structure
OR separately secured portion thereof
With intent to commit a crime therein
Unless premises were open to public or actor was licensed or privileged to enter
mandatory_minimum: 42 Pa.C.S. § 9714: 10-year mandatory minimum for second or subsequent conviction of crime of violence
enhancements: Felony 1 if building is adapted for overnight accommodation (whether or not anyone present)
Mandatory minimum under § 9714 for repeat violent offenders
notes: Pennsylvania burglary grading depends on whether the structure is adapted for overnight accommodation, not whether a person is present at time of entry.

elements: Entered a building adapted for overnight accommodation
With intent to commit a crime therein
A person was present at the time of entry
enhancements: Higher mandatory minimum under § 9714 for prior crime of violence

elements: Entered a building not adapted for overnight accommodation
With intent to commit a crime therein

statute_title: Unauthorized Use of Automobiles and Other Vehicles
offense_class: Misdemeanor 2; Felony 3 if vehicle not returned within 24 hours
elements: Operated another person's automobile, airplane, motorcycle, motorboat, or other motor-propelled vehicle
Without consent of the owner
OR knowingly received the vehicle knowing it to have been taken without consent
enhancements: Felony 3: theft of a motor vehicle under general theft statute (18 Pa.C.S. § 3921)
notes: Pennsylvania has separate unauthorized use (M2) and theft of vehicle (F3 under general theft statute) charges.

offense_class: Same grading as theft based on value
elements: Intentionally received, retained, or disposed of movable property of another
Knowing that it had been stolen
OR believing that it had probably been stolen
Unless at the time of receiving the actor intended to restore it to the owner
notes: Pennsylvania has a dedicated receiving stolen property statute with same grading tiers as theft.

offense_class: Summary (under $150); Misdemeanor 3 ($150-$500); Misdemeanor 2 ($500-$5,000); Misdemeanor 1 ($5,000+); Felony 3 (over $5,000 by explosion, flood, or aircraft)
elements: Intentionally or recklessly tampered with tangible property of another
So as to endanger person or property
OR intentionally or recklessly caused pecuniary loss to another by defrauding a public utility
enhancements: Felony 3 for destruction by explosion, flood, or aircraft causing damage over $5,000
notes: Pennsylvania calls this 'Criminal Mischief' not vandalism.

offense_class: Felony 3 (buildings); Misdemeanor 1 (defiance of order); Misdemeanor 3 (simple trespass)
elements: Knowing that not licensed or privileged to do so
Entered or remained in any place as to which notice against trespass had been given
enhancements: Felony 3: entering a building with intent to commit a crime (must be distinct from burglary) or breaking into a building
notes: Pennsylvania Criminal Trespass is graded more seriously than many states — entering a building can be a Felony 3.

offense_class: Summary to Felony 3 based on damage amount
elements: Intentionally or recklessly damaged tangible property of another person
OR tampered with property to endanger persons
notes: Pennsylvania's Criminal Mischief statute covers both vandalism and more serious property destruction.

statute_title: Simple Assault / Aggravated Assault — Domestic Violence
offense_class: Misdemeanor 2 to Felony 1 depending on injury and weapon
elements: Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to a family or household member
OR placed such person in fear of imminent serious bodily injury
enhancements: Mandatory arrest (18 Pa.C.S. § 2711) when reasonable grounds to believe domestic assault occurred
Enhanced penalties for second+ offense
Protection from Abuse order available under 23 Pa.C.S. § 6101
notes: Pennsylvania does not have a separate 'domestic violence' crime — assault charges are used with domestic violence designation for sentencing and mandatory arrest purposes.

elements: Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly caused bodily injury to a family or household member
enhancements: Mandatory arrest provision applies (18 Pa.C.S. § 2711)
Protection from Abuse (PFA) order typically issued
notes: Pennsylvania calls this Simple Assault in a domestic context. Mandatory arrest applies when physical injury is visible or credibly alleged.

offense_class: Misdemeanor 1; Felony 3 (course of conduct or serious bodily injury)
elements: As parent, guardian, or other person supervising child under 18
Knowingly endangered welfare of child by violating duty of care, protection, or support
OR, as adult, engaged in sexual activity or cohabited with person who committed child abuse
enhancements: Felony 3: course of conduct or child suffered serious bodily injury

offense_class: Felony 1 (serious bodily injury); Felony 2 (serious bodily injury attempt)
elements: Caused serious bodily injury to a child
Intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to child welfare
enhancements: Pennsylvania Child Protective Services Law (23 Pa.C.S. § 6301) mandates reporting
Pattern of child abuse: additional charges under § 6303
notes: Child abuse charges prosecuted under criminal assault statutes. Child Protective Services Law governs civil reporting requirements.

statute_title: Violation of Protection from Abuse Order
elements: A Protection from Abuse (PFA) order was in effect
Defendant had notice of the order
Defendant violated any provision of the order
enhancements: Felony 3: violation involving use of weapon
Each violation is a separate offense
notes: Pennsylvania PFA orders are issued under the Protection from Abuse Act (23 Pa.C.S. § 6101 et seq.).

offense_class: Misdemeanor 1 (1st offense); Felony 3 (2nd+ offense or with court order in place)
elements: On more than one occasion
Engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
With intent to cause substantial emotional distress to the person
OR with intent to place the person in reasonable fear of bodily injury
enhancements: Felony 3: second or subsequent offense, or defendant previously convicted of violent crime against victim

elements: With intent to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
Struck, shoved, kicked, or otherwise subjected them to physical contact
OR followed them in public
OR engaged in a course of conduct or repeated acts which serve no legitimate purpose
enhancements: Misdemeanor 3 for course of conduct involving communication in obscene language

offense_class: Misdemeanor 2; Felony 3 (great bodily harm or pattern of conduct)
elements: Knowingly endangered the welfare of a care-dependent person
By repeatedly failing to provide essential care or treatment
OR by abusing that person
enhancements: Felony 3: course of conduct or great bodily injury results
Financial exploitation: separate offense under 18 Pa.C.S. § 3922 (theft by deception)
notes: Pennsylvania Older Adults Protective Services Act (35 P.S. § 10225.101) runs parallel to criminal prosecution.

statute_title: Persons Not to Possess Firearms / Carrying Firearm Without License
offense_class: Felony 2 (persons not to possess); Felony 3 (carrying without license)
elements: Possessed a firearm
While being a person prohibited from possessing firearms under 18 Pa.C.S. § 6105
OR carried a firearm in a vehicle or concealed without a valid license to carry (§ 6106)
enhancements: Mandatory minimum 42 Pa.C.S. § 9712 if firearm visible during crime
notes: Pennsylvania requires a License to Carry Firearms (LTCF) issued by county sheriff for concealed or vehicle carry.

statute_title: Persons Not to Possess, Use, Manufacture, Control, Sell or Transfer Firearms
elements: Convicted of enumerated offense (including any felony, misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment over 2 years, domestic violence misdemeanor)
Possessed, used, manufactured, controlled, sold, or transferred a firearm
enhancements: Mandatory minimum under 42 Pa.C.S. § 9712 if firearm used in connection with another crime
notes: Pennsylvania § 6105 is broader than federal law — includes persons convicted of misdemeanors punishable by over 2 years and domestic violence misdemeanants.

statute_title: Firearms Not to Be Carried Without a License
elements: Carried a firearm in a vehicle or concealed on or about person
Without a valid License to Carry Firearms (LTCF)
In any city of the first class (Philadelphia), in a vehicle, or in a place where carrying is restricted
enhancements: Misdemeanor 1 exception if person had right to possess firearm but simply lacked LTCF
notes: Pennsylvania LTCF issued by county sheriff or chief of police. Philadelphia has additional restrictions. Open carry without LTCF is generally legal except in Philadelphia.

statute_title: Discharge of Firearm into an Occupied Structure
elements: Intentionally discharged a firearm
Into an occupied structure
Under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
enhancements: Additional charges for Reckless Endangerment (18 Pa.C.S. § 2705)

offense_class: Felony 2 (sale to prohibited person); Misdemeanor 2 (procedural violations)
elements: Sold, transferred, or delivered a firearm
To a person prohibited under 18 Pa.C.S. § 6105
OR without conducting required background check through dealer
enhancements: Straw purchase: additional federal charges often accompany state charges

elements: Possessed, made, repaired, sold, or otherwise dealt in a prohibited offensive weapon
Including bombs, grenades, machine guns, sawed-off shotguns, blackjacks, sandbags, metal knuckles, or other weapons of destruction

statute_title: Firearms Not to Be Carried Without a License
elements: Carried a firearm in a vehicle or concealed on person
In any city of the first class or while in a vehicle anywhere in Pennsylvania
Without a valid License to Carry Firearms
notes: Same as concealed-carry-violation for Pennsylvania. Licensed to Carry Firearms (LTCF) is required for concealed carry and vehicle carry statewide.

statute_title: Deceptive Business Practices / Wire Fraud (state equivalent)
elements: Used electronic communications to further a scheme to defraud
With intent to defraud another person of money or property
notes: Wire fraud in Pennsylvania is typically prosecuted federally under 18 U.S.C. § 1343. State-level prosecution uses theft by deception or deceptive business practices statutes.

offense_class: Misdemeanor 1 (under $2,000); Felony 3 ($2,000 to $100,000); Felony 2 (over $100,000 or victim 60+)
elements: Possesses or uses, through any means, identifying information of another person
Without the consent of that other person
To further any unlawful purpose
enhancements: Felony 2: victim is 60 years of age or older or amount over $100,000

statute_title: Theft by Failure to Make Required Disposition of Funds (Embezzlement)
offense_class: Same as theft based on amount
elements: Obtained property of another
Upon agreement or legal obligation to make specified payment or other disposition
Intentionally dealt with the property contrary to the agreement or legal obligation
notes: Pennsylvania uses 'Theft by Failure to Make Required Disposition' for the embezzlement concept.

offense_class: Felony 2 (currency, money, securities, postage, revenue stamps); Felony 3 (public records, government instruments); Misdemeanor 1 (other writing)
elements: With intent to defraud or injure another
Altered any writing of another without authority
OR made, completed, executed, authenticated, issued, or transferred any writing purporting to be the act of another
OR uttered any writing known to be forged
Issued or passed a check or similar sight order for payment of money
When at the time of issuance the issuer did not have sufficient funds in or credit with the drawee
And the issuer knew the check would not be honored
Intentionally or knowingly presented false information to an insurance company
OR concealed information for the purpose of obtaining insurance benefits or proceeds
To which the person was not entitled
enhancements: Felony 2 if involves arson or healthcare fraud over $100,000

elements: Used an access device (credit card, debit card, account number)
To obtain money, goods, or services
Without authority of the cardholder
Conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Knowing the property represented proceeds of criminal activity
With intent to promote criminal activity, conceal the source or nature of proceeds, or avoid reporting requirements

offense_class: Same grading as theft based on value
elements: Intentionally obtained property of another by deception
Created or reinforced a false impression (including false statements of fact, law, or intention)
OR prevented another from acquiring information that would have affected decision
notes: Pennsylvania uses 'Theft by Deception' (18 Pa.C.S. § 3922) for most general fraud conduct.

statute_title: Theft by Deception / Access Device Fraud — Financial Institution
elements: Intentionally obtained funds from a financial institution by deception or unauthorized access
With intent to defraud
notes: Bank fraud typically prosecuted federally under 18 U.S.C. § 1344. State prosecution uses theft by deception or access device fraud.

elements: Engaged in sexual intercourse or deviate sexual intercourse with a complainant
Without the complainant's consent
enhancements: Rape (18 Pa.C.S. § 3121): Felony 1 — forcible compulsion or threat
Aggravated Indecent Assault (18 Pa.C.S. § 3125): Felony 2
notes: Pennsylvania has separate offense tiers: Rape (F1, with force), Sexual Assault (F2, without consent), and Aggravated Indecent Assault (F2).

elements: Engaged in sexual intercourse with a complainant
By forcible compulsion or threat of forcible compulsion
OR by administering a drug or intoxicant that substantially impaired ability to resist
OR complainant was unconscious or unaware intercourse was occurring
OR complainant was less than 13 years of age
enhancements: Rape of child under 13: Felony 1 with 10-year mandatory minimum
SORNA registration required
notes: Pennsylvania retains 'rape' as a distinct offense title at Felony 1.

offense_class: Misdemeanor 2 (basic); Misdemeanor 1 (in presence of minor under 16)
elements: Exposed genitals in any public place
OR exposed genitals in any place where there were present other persons under circumstances in which the actor knew or should have known the conduct was likely to offend, affront, or alarm
enhancements: Misdemeanor 1 if person present was under 16 years of age
SORNA registration required for second offense or if minor victim

offense_class: Summary (patronizing a prostitute); Misdemeanor 2 (soliciting or promoting)
elements: Hired a prostitute or patronized prostitution
OR offered money or consideration to engage in sexual activity
enhancements: Felony 3: patronizing a prostitute who is under 18 (trafficking provisions apply)
notes: Pennsylvania recently revised prostitution laws to focus prosecution on traffickers and buyers rather than persons who sell sex.

offense_class: Felony 3 (contact); Felony 1 or 2 if underlying sexual offense would be F1/F2
penalty_max: 7 years (F3); up to 20 years if underlying F1 offense
elements: Intentionally contacted a minor
For purpose of engaging in activity prohibited by law
Including via the internet, telephone, or any other means
enhancements: Same grade as underlying sexual offense targeted
SORNA registration required

elements: Photographed, videotaped, depicted, or recorded a minor engaging in sexual act
OR distributed or exhibited such material
OR knowingly possessed such material
enhancements: SORNA Tier III (lifetime registration) for production
Mandatory consecutive sentences for multiple victims

statute_title: Failure to Comply with Registration of Sexual Offenders Requirements
elements: Required to register as a sex offender under Pennsylvania's SORNA (Subchapter H or I)
Failed to register, verify, or provide required information within required timeframe
enhancements: Felony 2 for second or subsequent failure to comply
notes: Pennsylvania's SORNA (Sexual Offender Registration and Notification Act) was substantially revised by Act 29 of 2018.

offense_class: Felony 2 (4-8 year age gap); Felony 1 (11+ year age gap)
elements: Engaged in sexual intercourse with a complainant under 16 years of age
Defendant is four or more years older than the complainant
Complainant and defendant are not married to each other
enhancements: Felony 1: defendant is 11 or more years older than victim
SORNA registration required
notes: Pennsylvania uses 'Statutory Sexual Assault' not 'statutory rape.' Age gap determines grading.

elements: Without the complainant's consent
Engaged in penetration, however slight, of the genitals or anus of the complainant with part of the defendant's body
enhancements: Felony 1 if victim is under 13 years of age

elements: With indecent contact with another person
Without the person's consent
OR with person who is substantially impaired, incapacitated, or under 13
enhancements: Misdemeanor 1: indecent contact with person under 16
Felony 3: victim is under 13, or defendant previously convicted of sex offense
notes: Pennsylvania calls this 'Indecent Assault' — equivalent to sexual battery in other states.

offense_class: Summary; Misdemeanor 3 (intent to cause substantial harm or serious inconvenience)
elements: With intent to cause public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm, or recklessly creating risk thereof
Engaged in fighting or threatening, or in violent or tumultuous behavior
OR made unreasonable noise
OR used obscene language or made an obscene gesture
OR created hazardous or physically offensive condition

statute_title: Resisting Arrest or Other Law Enforcement
elements: With the intent to prevent a public servant from effecting a lawful arrest or discharging any other duty
Created a substantial risk of bodily injury to the public servant or anyone else
OR employed means justifying or requiring substantial force to overcome the resistance
enhancements: Aggravated Assault charge (F1 or F2) if officer is injured

statute_title: Obstructing Administration of Law or Other Governmental Function
elements: Intentionally obstructed, impaired, or perverted the administration of law
OR prevented or attempted to prevent a public servant from lawfully performing an official function
By means of intimidation, physical force or interference, breach of official duty, or any other unlawful act

Witness Intimidation (18 Pa.C.S. § 4952): Felony 3

elements: Misbehavior in presence of court or near thereto
Misbehavior of officers of court in official transactions
Disobedience or resistance to lawful process, judgment, decree, or order
notes: Courts have inherent contempt power. Criminal contempt is separate from civil contempt (coercive).

elements: Appeared in a public place manifestly under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance
To the degree that the person may endanger the person or other persons or property
OR annoy persons in the vicinity
notes: Pennsylvania criminal public intoxication (§ 5505) is a summary offense. Unlike Illinois, Pennsylvania retains it as a criminal violation.

statute_title: Loitering and Prowling at Night Time
elements: Loitered or prowled in a place at a time or in a manner not usual for law-abiding individuals
Under circumstances that warrant alarm for the safety of persons or property in the vicinity
Made unreasonable noise or engaged in tumultuous behavior
With intent to cause public inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm
notes: Pennsylvania consolidates disturbing the peace under Disorderly Conduct (18 Pa.C.S. § 5503).

elements: Released on bail or recognizance in connection with a criminal proceeding
Failed to appear as required
Without lawful excuse

statute_title: False Reports to Law Enforcement Authorities
offense_class: Misdemeanor 3 (basic); Misdemeanor 2 (false report of terrorism); Felony 3 (false report of terrorism causing evacuation)
elements: Reported to law enforcement authorities an offense or other incident within their concern
Knowing that such offense or incident did not occur
OR provided false information to law enforcement
enhancements: Felony 3: false report causing evacuation of building or transportation vehicle

offense_class: Misdemeanor 1 (basic); Felony 3 (threat to commit crime of violence with intent to terrorize)
elements: Communicated, directly or indirectly, a threat to
Commit any crime of violence with intent to terrorize another
OR cause evacuation of a building or place of assembly
OR otherwise cause serious public inconvenience
enhancements: Felony 3: threat causes evacuation or substantial disruption of school
notes: Pennsylvania calls criminal threats 'Terroristic Threats.' School threats are very aggressively prosecuted.

statute_title: Modification or Revocation of Order of Probation
penalty_max: Full imprisonment sentence for underlying offense
elements: Was serving a term of probation
Violated condition of probation
Court must find violation by preponderance of evidence at revocation hearing
enhancements: New criminal conviction during probation: strong presumption for revocation
notes: Pennsylvania probation revocation hearings are before the sentencing judge. Commonwealth v. Simmons governs procedural requirements.

elements: Failed to report to probation officer
Failed to pay restitution or fines
Failed to complete community service
Failed drug or alcohol test
OR other non-criminal condition violation
notes: Pennsylvania legislature enacted Act 115 of 2019 requiring judges to consider graduated sanctions before imprisoning for technical probation violations.

statute_title: Substantive Violation of Probation — New Offense
elements: Committed a new criminal offense while on probation
New offense established by preponderance or separate criminal conviction
enhancements: Revocation and imposition of original sentence is presumptive for new felony during probation

offense_class: Administrative — Pennsylvania Board of Probation and Parole proceeding
penalty_max: Return to prison for remainder of sentence
elements: Released on parole by PBPP
Violated conditions of parole (new offense, absconder, failed drug test, etc.)
enhancements: New crime during parole: mandatory return to prison plus new sentence consecutive
notes: Pennsylvania has a Board of Probation and Parole (PBPP) that handles state parole violations. County probation violations are handled by courts.

penalty_max: Return to PDOC for balance of sentence
elements: Released on state parole or supervision
Violated conditions of supervision
notes: Pennsylvania uses 'parole' not 'supervised release.' PBPP handles state-level violations.

offense_class: Same grade as most serious offense that is object of conspiracy
elements: With intent of promoting or facilitating commission of a crime
Agreed with another person that they or one of them would engage in conduct which constitutes such crime
OR agreed to aid such other person in the planning or commission of such crime
enhancements: Pennsylvania conspiracy is graded same as the target offense (not one class lower like Illinois)
Overt act required only if conspiracy is Misdemeanor 1 or lower
notes: Pennsylvania conspiracy is graded the same as the underlying offense, unlike Illinois which grades it one class lower.

fine_max: $25,000 or three times the gain from the violation
elements: Was employed by or associated with an enterprise
Conducted or participated in conduct of enterprise's affairs
Through a pattern of racketeering activity
OR through collection of unlawful debt
enhancements: Civil forfeiture of proceeds
Federal RICO (18 U.S.C. § 1962) often charged in parallel
notes: Pennsylvania's Corrupt Organizations statute (18 Pa.C.S. § 911) is the state-level RICO equivalent.

statute_title: Use of Force in Self-Protection — Affirmative Defense
offense_class: Justification defense — not a criminal charge
elements: Defendant believed use of force was immediately necessary
To protect themselves against use of unlawful force by another
Belief was not reckless or negligent and force used was not excessive
notes: Pennsylvania Castle Doctrine codified at 18 Pa.C.S. § 505(b)(2.1) — no duty to retreat in dwelling or workplace. Stand Your Ground: no duty to retreat if not the initial aggressor.
